Initial Assessment Stage: The Initial Assessment Stage, is the first stage in a health emergency. In this stage, the model will run tests from the Early Action List to help identify probable diagnoses.
Diagnosis Stage: In the Diagnoses Stage, the model will read the crew member’s Medical Information to create a list of Probable Diagnoses. Next, the model will split the diagnoses into two categories: High Severity and Low Severity. Then it will rank the diagnoses such that the #1 diagnosis in each category is the most probable diagnosis.
Differential Diagnosis Stage: In the Differential Diagnosis Stage, the model will read the crew member’s Medical Information and search the available actions to determine which tests will help confirm or eliminate the possible diagnoses. In this stage, the model will prioritize the High Severity diagnoses.
Intervention Stage: In the Initial Intervention Stage, the model will use the Medical Information to determine whether the crew member should receive treatment and, if so, what treatment they need.
Monitoring Stage: In the Monitoring Stage, the model can schedule a check-up exam for a later time or order follow-up tests.
Stable Health Stage: The Stable Health Stage, is the last stage in a health emergency. After reading a crew member’s Medical Information, the model can pick the Stable Health Stage if it has determined that the crew member is stable or if there is nothing more you can do.
